Hypothesis: with the same workload and warmed/cold-cache state, GDS reduces host-memory staging and checkpoint completion time without increasing p99 I/O latency or compromising recovery; this is falsifiable.

First verify vendor-supported GDS/filesystem/kernel combinations, mount options, permissions, GPU-direct capability, peer access, IOMMU/container settings, and that the application actually selects the direct path. Compare GDS with a CPU-staged baseline using identical data, ranks, synchronization, cache state, and repetition; report units, distributions, confidence intervals, and per-node outliers. Do not infer GPU-DMA benefit from aggregate storage throughput alone.

Inject an authorized interruption and a node failure during checkpoint write, then verify atomic visibility, checksums, manifest/rank completeness, restart from the last committed checkpoint, and cleanup of partial files. Roll back to CPU staging if any supported-path check fails, checksum/metadata validation fails, restart cannot reproduce progress, p99 latency exceeds the agreed SLO, or checkpoint time regresses beyond the predeclared threshold. Evidence required: version/configuration capture, direct-path trace or counters, synchronized per-rank metrics, baseline results, and failure-test logs.
